items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the racing, pari-mutuel wagering and breeding law, in relation
to health insurance for New York trainers at franchised corporation race
tracks
items.lawSection: Racing, Pari-Mutuel Wagering and Breeding Law
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4549

SPONSOR: ADDABBO
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the racing, pari-mutuel wagering and breeding law, in
relation to health insurance for New York trainers at franchised corpo-
ration race tracks

 
PURPOSE:

To establish a health insurance program for thoroughbred trainers at the
franchised corporation which shall be modeled upon the existing health
insurance program that is currently offered to jockeys and contained in
section 221-a of the racing, pari-mutuel wagering and breeding law

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Establishes a new subsection 221-b within the racing, pari-
mutuel wagering and breeding law which shall be established through
industry revenue received up to four percent of the gross purse enhance-
ment amount from video lottery gaming at aqueduct racetrack.

Section 2: Establishes that NYRA and NYTHA must enter into a MOD that
sets forth the parameters for operating and qualifying for the program
along with setting forth basic requirements that the program must offer.
This section also sets forth the role and responsibilities of the Gaming
Commission in overseeing the program.

Section 3. Effective Date shall be immediately, provided that premiums
shall begin no later than 60 days following the approval of the MOD
between NYRA and NYTHA and approved by the Gaming Commission.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation will provide health insurance to thoroughbred trainers
who have been hit hard by the COVID-19 pandemic.If enacted, this legis-
lation will provide an incentive for thoroughbred trainers to keep their
business operations in New York State. It will also help additional
individuals receive health insurance.

This legislation will also help the thoroughbred racing industry grow
and expand. It will led to more starts at the franchised corporation
circuit. Additional starts at the franchised corporation will led to
higher handle and increased tax revenue to the State of New York.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

This legislation will be financed by racing support payments that is
received by the thoroughbred racing industry and will not have any
fiscal impact upon the State of New York.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
